answer.rationale: Finance mandates an 18% cut and the incumbent has already refused to reopen price this cycle, which forecloses negotiate_terms as a viable lever right now (contradicts the premise behind memory_c4, which I'd want the archived record on before ruling it out entirely). Memory_c2 suggests switching primary vendor previously cut unit cost sharply with quick, clean onboarding, which is the only path likely to meet the cost mandate — but I verify it rather than trust it outright because that record is from a different time and the current line is at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, so any onboarding friction this time could trigger delivery misses, unlike the prior instance. Given the 14-day contract expiry and no auto-renew, a full broad-rollout switch is too risky to commit blind; a small guarded test (e.g., partial volume shift or parallel qualification) lets us start the cost-reduction move without betting the whole committed volume on unverified onboarding speed. Renewing incumbent as-is fails the cost mandate outright, deferring isn't available since the contract lapses in 14 days, and add_second_source doesn't address the imminent expiry of the primary contract, so it's deprioritized to next cycle.
